newsitem.title: USA: Dell Computer sees no sign of PC price war.
newsitem.headline: Dell Computer sees no sign of PC price war.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp Senior Vice President Kevin Rollins said on Friday the company saw no sign of an imminent price war in the personal computer industry.
"We have not seen any extraordinary price moves by our competitors. We believe most everyone has behaved very rationally," Rollins said at the company's annual shareholder meeting in Austin.
Rollins said price cuts in the PC industry have traditionally followed reductions in the cost of components and that was still the case.
"We haven't seen anything that would make us believe that there has been a change," he said.

Analysts have forecast a price war as chief rival Compaq Computer Co shifts to a build-to-order, direct-sales distribution strategy, challenging Dell's position as the leading direct-sales PC company.
Dell Chairman Michael Dell told Reuters after the meeting that "a price war is when the price has come down faster than costs. That's not happening."
Dell shareholders approved a two-for-one stock split authorized by the company's board in May to be paid on July 25 as a 100 percent stock dividend to shareholders of record on Friday.
